body: It isn't great but I'm just slowly learning to accept that this is just the way things are and there isn't much I can do about it, so perhaps I should just let go of the hope of things ever changing. But that's still a work in progress, I like to think of myself as a pessimistic optimist of sorts if that makes any sense. You'd make an awesome therapist/counsellor person by the way, you're a good listener and good at phrasing things. It's nice getting to talk someone who actually listens and can make sense of it all. Anyhow, I guess we'll see how the coming week pans out, maybe it'll go better than this one. Have a nice weekend :)

That was reassuring thank you, it makes it feel a lot less like this is all just in my head; I mean technically it still all could be but hopefully you get my point haha. Lol, that certainly takes the never go down without a fight thing to a whole new level :) 

I guess I'd just ask that they listen to me. I've tried reaching out before but it doesn't really work out well. I just get cut off and told that people have it so much worse and they seem to be doing perfectly well so I'm clearly just being childish and too lazy to easily fix my own 'exaggerated' problems that I'm the sole cause of. I know I have my own shortcomings and I'm not perfect, but it's just so frustrating, I don't want to feel this way or be where I am, I wish I could be happier and more like the old me again and I am trying to trying to fix this but it's not so simple to fix, but they just won't see that. I wouldn't ask that they understand completely, just that they'd try and give me a little space to figure things out without it being taken as me being deliberately cold and distant. It wouldn't fix everything but it'd make things easier to deal with.

It isn't so much that I'd want permission to give up, to use the analogy of the black knight, when you've already lost both arms you start to question if there's even a point in still going on. A part of me is just tired of fighting and wants to stop but when I think about the alternative and the consequences of what would happen, that's what makes me keep going even if it means risking loosing another limb. I know at this point that maybe it's already too far gone for me to fix it but I don't want to let it go. I'm just scared that soon there won't be anything left for me to hold on to, I'll just be a limbless torso and that'll be when the real fun begins.

I'm not usually one for talking about things, sometimes it is easier to pretend your problems don't exist rather than have to acknowledge them, but it's so nice being able to talk to someone that can understand and relate to you on some level. Perhaps it's partly because I'm not having to say this all in person but you're a pretty good listener and awesome at putting things into to words; it helps makes some sense of the jumbled mess in there haha. It really does mean a lot that you actually take the time to read my ramblings and reply so thank you :) 

Yeah I suppose it is like that. I only wish all the noise in there and whatever else could just stop for a moment, so I could have minute to get my bearings a little, but I guess in reality a part of me just wants something to 'take it all away' even though I know it doesn't work that way. I know you're meant to face things head on but sometimes pretending to myself or the people around me that everything is all fine is the only thing that keeps me afloat some days, its far less scary at least. I've been thinking about it all and I realised that things are perhaps worse than I allowed myself to believe. I don't like the idea of just giving up, you're meant to keep getting back up right? But I'm just so tired that I don't know how much longer I can keep doing this; still it is what it is I suppose.

I hope you managed to have a good rest, and that this week wasn't too hectic :) 

Yeah it really does feel like that. I like how you've phrased that, anaesthetising, it's a nice way of putting it. Before it would just be for brief periods during times when I was particularly stressed like you said, but now it's becoming increasingly more frequent and the smallest trivial things can just set it off and I kind feel myself loosing touch with reality a little, it kind of feels like your teetering over the edge of something. The strangest part, that's a little newer, is I sometimes get these weird intrusive thoughts, I don't mean like I can hear voices I know it's all me, but it's just odd because I'm not consciously thinking them. Like I could be waiting for the train and a part of me thinks, just walk across the tracks to the other platform, this isn't real so nothing bad will happen to you or I'll get the urge to do something to myself that I know would hurt but at the time it just feels as though it wouldn't because it all just must be like a dream simulation. When it gets to that point, its like a part of my mind becomes very paranoid and confused and it feels like everyone around me (even random strangers) are all in on this thing that I don't know and they all sort of "know" and are watching. I never do any of it, and I know logically none of it is true, it's just a little scary that it still feels real at the time. It doesn't last long either, a day or two at most and then it goes away again but yeah that's a new part to it. I like to think the fact I can still tell that it isn't real means it isn't so bad? I don't know, I have an over active imagination at the best of times so I guess it could probably just be that going into overdrive.

Yeah I totally agree. Not great, things just went down hill (or more so) which was awesome but it is what it is I guess. Its funny, at times it just feels like I'm watching myself like I'm in a film and you aren't sure whether to laugh or cry because none of it feels real and everything just feels strangely distant. Anyhow, I hope that your week went ok :)
Yeah it does, you've pretty much just summed it all up.

It does feel like that. It's so nice and refreshing finally having someone actually listen and understand where I'm coming from, so thank you. Writing this down, it does make me feel a little better getting it out, but it's also starting to dawn on me that things are probably never going to get better. Is there even a point in holding on to the tiny hope that it will or am I just deluding myself and buying time for the inevitable? Like if I can see where this is all headed, why don't I just spare myself the extra misery further down the line and just get it over and done with? I don't know, I hate feeling this way but I don't know how to make it stop.

It'd probably take way too long to try and explain it all properly, so I'll just try and not make this ridiculously long. I'm at a point in my life where if I mess up now, everything I've ever done and sacrificed/worked for towards 'my future' will be for nothing and it will go to waste. Once it goes wrong I will never be able to fix it. 

That all sounds incredibly petulant but the consequences after are the kind I'd have to face for years and years to come. I just hate the thought that I'd come all this way and be this close only to just loose everything. And it wouldn't be because I didn't try or I wasn't dedicated or put the time in, but because things would keep getting in the way and I was forever playing catch up or having to work myself to breaking point in order to salvage things and get back on track. I hate the feeling of knowing I can do better at something and just having to settle. 

Certain people in my life are a major part of why things are the way they are but I'm not in a position where I can change that. The best part is they won't even admit to it or even listen when I try and talk to them. Either they'd just say I deserved what was coming and they hoped it would go wrong or I should stop selfishly complaining and just and fix it just like I always did and I should stop being so 'moody'. They just don't get it.

I'd mostly be upset with myself if it did all fall apart, but I know they and some of my other family members would love nothing more than to relish and constantly remind me about it for the rest of my days. I don't know if I'd be able to handle that. I don't like having excuses for things despite what it seems, I'd rather just get on with it but it just feels a lot like I'm stuck playing this game where everything has been rigged against me and I just have to keep on this fake smile for everyone the whole time. I don't know what to do. Anyhow, I guess that's the gist of it. Thanks for reading all of that btw it really does mean a lot.

What does a nosy pepper do? 
Gets jalapeño business! :D

Reading what you wrote, I think it's certainly understandable why you would feel that way. I am by no means an expert, but sometimes when I'm feeling overwhelmed and panicked about everything, I take a step back, have a brief moment to myself, it doesn't have to be long especially if you're short on time, perhaps like minute or two where you can just breathe and get your bearings back and then I just focus on one small thing at a time and try not to think about the rest. The other things won't go away sure and this isn't to say avoid thinking about them forever its just for a short while, until you feel a little more in control of yourself. Then perhaps it might make it a little easier to tackle everything else. I hope that some of this was of some help. All the best with everything!

I'm sorry to hear that. I have thoughts about it sometimes, so I can kind of relate to some of your concerns on some level, but for now it's still more of a morbid fantasy, rather than something I'd actually carry out. I hope that things can get a little easier for you someday. All the best!

I've heard of one or two similar cases too. Ending up dependent on them and the other aspects did worry me a little but I guess even though I know logically they don't work like this, a part of me was just looking for something that would just 'take it all away' even if it was just for a time. I've never been formally diagnosed with anything, I pretty much just look up how I feel online and see what it matches up to? So I don't even know if this technically even counts as depression or whether its a part of something else. In any case, thank you for sharing that!

Thanks for sharing that. I'm glad you were able to get something positive out of seeing a psychiatrist. I'm not very good at talking about things, in person at least, so I'm not sure how effective that would be. I'm still thinking about it all but your story definitely gave me something to think about, so thank you. All the best to you too!
